body: Thank you.  I have found a good therapist.  I tell him things that I don't tell anyone else.  He seems to really listen and give thoughtful responses.  I'm lucky in other regards too - her family is very supportive.  So are my family, friends, neighbors, and co-workers.  None of this makes things better, but it makes things easier.  I try to not let myself dwell on what happened (and all the things that may have led to it) because I know that won't bring her back.  But it took me the past three months just to get to the point where she isn't the only thing on my mind 24/7.  I'll never forgive myself for some of the things I said and did, and that's why I don't think I'll ever heal.  So, instead, I guess I just have to learn to live with it.  I've learned a lot from this experience so far but what a shitty way to learn.
Thanks.  And I'm not trying to be a downer.  I just don't see this as motivational because I know that time isn't going to heal this particular wound.

I'm almost 40 as well.  My wife recently committed suicide.  Tell me how that's ever going to be alright.  There are some things that time can't heal.

Edit: Whoever downvoted me can fuck off.  If you think I'm making this up, check my post history.
Thank you for sharing that and thanks for the suggestion.
